shortDescription: Contract manufacturer Flex NASDAQ:FLEX said on Thursday it will acquire power conversion systems maker EPC Power in a deal valued at $4.4 billion to strengthen its position in AI data center and power infrastructure markets.Here are more details:

children: said on Thursday it will acquire power conversion systems maker EPC Power in a deal valued at $4.4 billion to strengthen its position in AI data center and power infrastructure markets.
Flex said the deal will expand its Cloud and Power Infrastructure (CPI) business as demand for AI infrastructure and next-generation 800V data center power systems grows.
Flex CEO Revathi Advaithi said EPC Power's power conversion and grid-forming technology will help Flex benefit from the shift to next-generation power systems.
The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, after which EPC Power will become part of Flex's Cloud and Power Infrastructure (CPI) segment.
Flex said it intends to separate its CPI segment into a standalone public company in the first quarter of 2027.
Flex said it expects to finance the acquisition through a combination of debt and equity, with committed financing provided by Citi and Bank of America.
EPC Power develops power conversion systems used in data centers, energy storage projects and electric grids.
The company has deployed more than 15 gigawatts of power systems in 62 countries and expects its U.S. manufacturing capacity to exceed 30 gigawatts in 2027.
